question: Should WhatsApp intentionally fail closed for injected media readers without explicit local roots while making the new base64 and widened media APIs supported Plugin SDK contracts?
rationale: The code can establish that the shared boundary is safer and internally consistent, but automation cannot decide whether the upgrade-visible failure mode and permanent third-party API surface are accepted product contracts.

options.title: Approve canonical boundary
options.body: Accept the explicit-root requirement and focused SDK additions, then land after confirming the audited callers and compatibility tests cover the intended upgrade behavior.

options.title: Add a transition contract
options.body: Preserve a narrowly documented, deprecated explicit opt-in for legacy all-roots readers and remove it on a stated schedule.

options.title: Narrow or split the SDK surface
options.body: Keep the WhatsApp security migration but defer public helpers that are not yet justified as stable third-party contracts.

recommendation.title: Approve canonical boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the explicit-root requirement and focused SDK additions, then land after confirming the audited callers and compatibility tests cover the intended upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest demonstrated ownership of the WhatsApp and media surfaces and authored the coordinated boundary migration.
